guards.what: BLOAT places the spawned Gas Bomb in the wrong enemy-list position
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-28: BLOAT now places the Gas Bomb in its encounter slot. living_fog.py gives GasBomb a `slot` field, picks the first free bombN slot (the port of Encounter.GetNextSlot, EncounterModel.cs:245-248, over LivingFogNormal.Slots = [bomb1..bomb5, livingFog], LivingFogNormal.cs:18) and calls `CreatureCmd.add(ctx.hooks, bomb, index=idx)` where idx is the first enemy holding a HIGHER slot index (_slot_index gives the Living Fog 5) -- reproducing CombatManager.AddCreature -> CombatState.SortEnemiesBySlotName (CombatState.cs:495-501). EXECUTED on a real LIVING_FOG_NORMAL combat driven through ADVANCED_GAS then BLOAT: enemies after BLOAT = ['GasBomb', 'LivingFog'], Gas Bomb at index 0, so the bomb's DEATH_BLOW resolves before the Fog's move. WAS: an index-less CreatureCmd.add that APPENDED, giving ['LivingFog','GasBomb'] -- wrong enemy turn order and a positional 'enemies' divergence in replay. The sort is not a random draw, so this holds on the legacy/RL path too.
guards.rationale: EXECUTED, `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b03.py slot-order`, a real CombatState driven through ADVANCED_GAS then BLOAT: 'SIM enemies after BLOAT : [LivingFog, GasBomb]' / 'GAME enemies after BLOAT : [GasBomb, LivingFog] (slot sort over [bomb1..bomb5, livingFog])'; 'sim next enemy turn acts in order: [LivingFog, GasBomb]' vs 'game next enemy turn acts in order: [GasBomb, LivingFog]'; 'sim index of the Gas Bomb: 1' vs 'game index of the Gas Bomb: 0'. LIVE under rule 6, both sides proved reachable on ported content: 'living_fog' is in the Underdocks normal-encounter pool (rooms.py:201, re-verified 2026-08-04, was :135, unchanged), the encounter is LIVING_FOG_NORMAL (living_fog.py:101-104), and the code path is taken on the second Living Fog turn of every such fight - BLOAT_MOVE is a fixed link in a branchless chain, so it CANNOT be skipped, and the free-slot test passes on turn 2 because no bomb exists yet. Nothing unported is required.

guards.what: The free-slot test itself (how many bombs may be alive)
guards.rationale: Separate from the ordering gap and correct. GetNextSlot returns string.Empty only when every entry of Slots is occupied by a creature still in CombatState.Enemies (EncounterModel.cs:245-248), and the fog permanently holds 'livingFog', so the real cap is five LIVE bombs. living_fog.py:88-93 counts `isinstance(e, GasBomb) and not e.is_gone` and gates on `< 5` (_BOMB_SLOTS = 5, :18), which is the same predicate: an exploded bomb is removed from Enemies in the game (it vetoes neither ShouldDie nor ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath) and is is_gone in the sim, so both sides free the slot at the same moment. BloatAmount is a field initialised to 1 and written nowhere (LivingFog.cs:22,44-55), matching _BLOAT_SPAWNS = 1.
LivingFog.cs:89-101 runs the spawn loop and THEN the 5-damage attack; living_fog.py:88-95 does the same. Observable: a Thorns-style reaction to the attack would see the bomb already present.

LivingFog.cs:32-40, LAST argument: MinInitialHp 80 (MaxInitialHp = MinInitialHp), AdvancedGasDamage 8, BloatDamage 5, SuperGasBlastDamage 8; plus Smoggy 1 (:82) and BloatAmount 1 (:22). Sim living_fog.py:13-18, 55-56.

guards.what: GasBomb's EXPLODE_MOVE is a DeathBlowIntent, and only carried MoveType.DEATH_BLOW
guards.issue: Closed 2026-08-02: living_fog.py:51-52 now constructs `Intent(MoveType.DEATH_BLOW, damage=_EXPLODE_DMG, also=(MoveType.ATTACK,))`. WAS: `also` was empty, so `intent.has(MoveType.ATTACK)` read False for GasBomb's EXPLODE_MOVE. `DeathBlowIntent` (game src\Core\MonsterMoves\Intents\DeathBlowIntent.cs:10) is a `SingleAttackIntent` (:8 of SingleAttackIntent.cs) which is an `AttackIntent` (:8 of AttackIntent.cs); its own `IntentType` override returns `IntentType.DeathBlow`, not `IntentType.Attack` (DeathBlowIntent.cs:16), but `MonsterModel.IntendsToAttack` (MonsterModel.cs:241-245) explicitly ORs `IntentType.Attack` and `IntentType.DeathBlow` together for gameplay purposes, and that predicate gates `GoForTheEyes.OnPlay`'s Weak application (`src\Core\Models\Cards\GoForTheEyes.cs:49-52`: `if (cardPlay.Target.Monster.IntendsToAttack) { await PowerCmd.Apply<WeakPower>(...) }`) and its glow-gold targeting hint (`GoForTheEyes.cs:22-27`, `HittableEnemies.Any(e => e.Monster?.IntendsToAttack ?? false)`). It is also a real `AttackIntent` by C# class hierarchy, so `NIntent.cs:135`'s `intent is AttackIntent attackIntent` check renders its damage number like any other attack. Before the fix, playing Go For The Eyes into a GasBomb whose intent is EXPLODE never applied Weak and the observation's attack flag / damage preview for that intent were blank -- silently wrong both for the card's real effect and for the RL observation. Found by an RL task, not by this record's own audit (both were previously verdicted faithful without checking `also=`); see the sibling guard entry that swept for further sites of the same class.
guards.rationale: EXECUTED: `test/test_combat_obs_v4.py` gained a real Living Fog encounter test driving GasBomb to EXPLODE_MOVE and asserting the observation's attack flag/damage preview are populated; full suite green at 4399 passed / 6 xfailed / 0 failed after the fix. Confirmed independently by reading `DeathBlowIntent.cs`, `SingleAttackIntent.cs`, `AttackIntent.cs`, `MonsterModel.cs:241-245`, `GoForTheEyes.cs:22-27,49-52` and `NIntent.cs:135` in the game source, and `living_fog.py:38-56` in the sim, on 2026-08-02.
